draft.title: Transformers
card: A transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil wound on a shared iron core. An alternating current in the primary makes a changing magnetic flux in the core, which induces an emf in the secondary.
The voltages depend on the number of turns: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns. More turns on the secondary than the primary gives a higher voltage (step-up). Fewer turns gives a lower voltage (step-down).
A steady direct current gives a constant flux, so no emf is induced in the secondary. A transformer needs a changing current to work.
Power lines use high voltage. For the same power, a higher voltage means a smaller current, and less energy is lost as heat in the wires (P = I²R).
draft.remember: Voltage ratio matches turns ratio. High voltage means low current, so less heat lost in the lines.

a.q: A transformer has 200 turns on its primary coil and 1000 turns on its secondary coil. The primary is connected to a 12 V AC supply. What is the secondary voltage?
opts: 60 V, so it is a step-up transformer
60 V, so it is a step-down transformer
2.4 V, so it is a step-up transformer
2.4 V, so it is a step-down transformer
a.why: Vs = Vp × Ns/Np = 12 × 1000/200 = 60 V. The secondary has more turns, so the voltage is stepped up. 2.4 V comes from flipping the ratio.
a.clue: Which coil has more turns, and what does that do to the voltage?

b.q: A power station sends the same power along a long cable at 11 kV in one case and at 220 kV in the other. Why is less energy lost as heat at 220 kV?
opts: The current is smaller, so I²R heating is smaller
The cable resistance falls as the voltage rises
The current is larger, so the energy moves faster
The frequency changes, so the cable stays cooler
b.why: For the same power, P = VI, so a higher voltage means a smaller current. Heat loss is I²R, so it falls sharply. The cable's resistance does not change with the voltage applied to it, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Use P = VI first, then think about I²R.

a.best: 60 V, so it is a step-up transformer

b.best: The current is smaller, so I²R heating is smaller
